title: Malted Milk Ice Cream (No Egg)
changes_from_base: Malted milk powder flavours the base and crushed chocolate malt balls are folded in, instead of strawberries.
summary: A toasty, biscuit-like ice cream flavoured with malted milk powder and packed with crushed chocolate malt balls, like an old-fashioned malted shake.

ingredients.item: light corn syrup or glucose syrup
fine sea salt or table salt
chocolate-coated malted milk balls, roughly crushed

steps.title: Dissolve the malt
steps.text: Whisk the malted milk powder into the cold milk in the saucepan until no lumps remain, then add the sugar, syrup and salt.

steps.title: Warm
steps.text: Heat, whisking, until steaming and the sugar has dissolved; malt powder catches on the bottom if left alone, so keep it moving.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Pour into the jug, whisk in the cold cream and vanilla and chill for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Crush the malt balls
steps.text: Tap them in the freezer bag with the rolling pin into rough halves and quarters, then freeze until needed.

steps.title: Churn and finish
steps.text: Churn for 20-30 min, fold in the crushed malt balls and freeze, covered, for at least 4 h.

tips: Whisk the malt powder into cold milk first; added to hot milk it clumps.
Malt balls contain barley malt, so this is not gluten-free.
Serve between two biscuits for an ice-cream sandwich.
storage: Keep covered with baking paper pressed on the surface in the freezer for up to 2 weeks. Soften for 10 min in the fridge before scooping.
